requirement:
Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and
setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an
anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items
appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.sections`. I did not request any implementation source.

- **`section` kind and whitespace-normalized names.**
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` (`outline/tests.rs`) turns `# Head  *one*` into `section[Head%20*one*]`. It also checks that the structural hash survives reflowing the heading text.
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` turns `Heading   words` into `section[Heading%20words]`.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` turns the two-line setext text `Títle`/`two` into `section[Títle%20two]`.
- **ATX and setext headings.**
  - ATX is covered in `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading`, `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` and `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
  - Setext is covered by the `===` heading in `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble`.
  - Setext is also covered by the `---` level-two heading in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
  - A multi-line setext heading, with a literal `===` inside a fenced code block that must not become a heading, is covered by `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code`.
  - Setext headings inside a directive block, a quote and a list are covered by `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans`.
- **Anonymous preamble.** The requirement says content before the first heading "can" form an anonymous section, so this is optional. The tests still assert a `section@…` selector for the preamble in `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble`, `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` and `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`. The last two also check that front matter is skipped and that the preamble text is `préface`.
- **Nesting by heading level.**
  - A level-3 heading directly under a level-1 heading (`### Deep` under `# Main`) is covered.
  - Same-level siblings (`## Same` twice) are covered.
  - A return to a shallower level (`# End`) is covered.
  - A level-2 setext heading under `# End` is covered.
  - A later `## Peer` becomes a sibling of the setext section, not a child of it.
- **Other items beneath their nearest enclosing container.**
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` asserts the parent-index and line-range tuples for a section, a paragraph, a block and a nested block with its paragraph.
  - It also checks `owner_at_line`.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` asserts the selector prefix `section[End]/section[Level%20two]/block@` for a block.
  - `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans` asserts `/block@` in the selector only for the directive case.
- **Selectors under `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.** The encoding of `/ [ ] # @ %` and whitespace in `section[Main%20%2F%20%5Bx%5D%20%23%20%40%20%25%20end]` is asserted. Duplicate siblings get `#1` and `#2`. Anonymous nodes use `kind@` plus a 12-hex-digit hash. Selectors resolve back to nodes, and the selected text and span are checked against the source.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and
setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an
anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items
appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
